item.title: Trump announces Russia-Ukraine "energy ceasefire" after criticizing Zelenskyy
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia alone is responsible for the war in Ukraine, after President Trump said he should be replaced.

item.description: The following is the transcript of the interview with Senate Majority Whip John Barrasso, Republican of Wyoming, that aired on "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" on Oct. 11, 2026.

item.description: The following is the transcript of the interview with Sen. Chris Murphy, Democrat of Connecticut, that aired on "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" on Oct. 11, 2026.

item.title: Rep. Jeffries says Democrats are "on the verge of taking back control"
item.description: Jeffries campaigned in New Jersey and Pennsylvania and plans to campaign in Texas in the coming days to help Democratic candidates unseat Republican incumbents.

item.title: Gunman charged with killing officer, wounding another in West Philly
item.description: Eric Lewis faces several charges, including homicide of a law enforcement officer, in the shooting death of 40-year-old Shane Seiber.

item.title: Fugitive wanted for allegedly bribing Venezuelan officials taken in U.S. custody
item.description: Alvaro Pulido was indicted in Miami federal court in 2019 and again in 2021 as part of an investigation into his longtime business partner, Alex Saab​, a one-time ally of ousted President Nicolás Maduro.

item.title: Iran calls U.S. response "insufficient" amid stalled talks to end the war
item.description: After Saudi Arabia said Iran's Houthi allies carried out another strike at Riyadh's airport, Iran called the U.S. effort to negotiate toward ending the war "insufficient."

item.title: Terminal in Riyadh airport hit again, a day after deadly strike killed 12
item.description: The strike on King Khalid International Airport, the deadliest on Saudi soil in more than a decade, marked a major escalation in the war between Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis and the kingdom.

item.title: 60 Minutes travels to the West Bank as settler violence surges
item.description: With Israel's election two weeks away, Lesley Stahl travels to the West Bank, where militant Israeli settlers have carried out violent attacks against the Palestinians, often with impunity. The Israeli government is showing an unwillingness to crack down on the violence. Tonight on 60 Minutes.

item.title: Full transcript of "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan," Oct. 11, 2026
item.description: On this "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" broadcast, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin and Senate Majority Whip John Barrasso join Margaret Brennan.

item.title: DHS secretary defends livestream of Fort Hood shooter's execution
item.description: Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin defended the Pentagon's plan to livestream the execution of an ex-Army major who was convicted of the 2009 killing of 13 people at Fort Hood.

item.title: Palantir's Shyam Sankar suggests "human error," not AI, is cause of Iran school bombing
item.description: Palantir chief technology officer Shyam Sankar, on "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan," defended the military's use of artificial intelligence and said that he believes the final report on a bombing of a girls' school in Iran will show "the likely cause is human error."

item.title: Thousands still without power in Florida and Alabama as Isaias moves north
item.description: The storm, which hit as a Category 2 hurricane near Destin, Florida, has been linked to at least four deaths.

item.title: GOP Senate Majority Whip John Barrasso calls reports about Kimberly Guilfoyle "very troubling"
item.description: GOP Senate Majority Whip John Barrasso told "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" that "what we've seen in the reports is very troubling" about Kimberly Guilfoyle, the ambassador to Greece, allegedly asking Eric Deters to pay $100,000 of her debts to help her confirmation. "It's concerning and I'm sure there's going to be an investigation," he added.

item.title: Sen. Chris Murphy says Trump administration is "absolutely incompetent in war making"
item.description: Democratic Sen. Chris Murphy of Connecticut on "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" slammed the Trump administration for its handling of the Iran war, saying "if the Trump administration was trying to lose this war, they couldn't do worse than they are doing," adding he believes they are "absolutely incompetent in war making."

item.title: Face the Nation: Barrasso, Pappas, Sankar
item.description: Missed the second half of the show? GOP Senate Whip John Barrasso and Democratic Rep. Chris Pappas join. Plus, Palantir's Chief Technology Officer Shyam Sankar.

item.title: Democrat Chris Pappas says "we're taking nothing for granted" in N.H. race
item.description: Democratic Rep. Chris Pappas, who's running to represent New Hampshire in the Senate, said that "we're taking nothing for granted" as Election Day approaches, amid a "tough race" in the Granite State.

item.title: This week on "Sunday Morning" (Oct. 11)
item.description: A look at the features for this week's broadcast of the Emmy-winning program, hosted by Jane Pauley.

item.title: 10/11: Face The Nation
item.description: This week on "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan," U.S. Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin joins, along with Sens. John Barrasso, Chris Murphy and Democratic Senate candidate Rep. Chris Pappas. Plus, Palantir's Chief Technology Officer Shyam Sankar.

item.title: The girls of summer
item.description: Women's pro baseball has been largely inactive in this country since the pioneering All-American Girls Professional Baseball League folded 72 years ago. Now, with the new Women's Pro Baseball League (which debuted this summer), women are again taking to the diamond in a league of their own. Correspondent Faith Salie talks with #1 draft pick Kelsie Whitmore; catcher Maggie Foxx; commissioner Justine Siegal; and CEO Keith Stein about what the new league means for women and sports.

item.title: Billy Crystal on finding humor in the darkest of times
item.description: In January 2025, the Pacific Palisades wildfire burned more than 5,000 homes, including Billy Crystal's. From the smoldering ruins of what was once his family home, Crystal found inspiration for his latest one-man Broadway show, "860."

item.title: Extended interview: Noah Kahan
item.description: In this extended conversation, Luke Burbank talks with singer-songwriter Noah Kahan about how his home state of Vermont has inspired his music; dealing with stardom; the process of writing his latest album, "The Great Divide"; and founding his mental health non-profit, The Busyhead Project.

item.title: 10/11: Sunday Morning
item.description: Hosted by Jane Pauley. Featured: The life of Ethel Kennedy; Steve Bannon; Billy Crystal on his one-man Broadway show, "860"; singer-songwriter Noah Kahan; children's book author Julia Donaldson; women's baseball; and a proper paella.

item.title: Pope Leo to undergo surgery after nodular lesion found in lung, Vatican says
item.description: The American pope has no previously known health problems and is known to be physically active

item.title: DOJ investigating TV networks over suspension of press pool after Trump media ban
item.description: The Justice Department is investigating whether the major TV networks violated antitrust laws after they briefly suspended the TV press pool system in response to President Trump's decision to ban three news organizations from the White House.

item.title: Hundreds of thousands without power as Isaias makes landfall, kills at least 4
item.description: Hundreds of thousands of people are without power and dealing with debris cleanup after Isaias made landfall as a Category 2 Hurricane on Friday night. Jason Allen reports, and Grant Gilmore has the forecast.

item.title: 10/10: CBS Weekend News
item.description: Isaias kills at least 4 in Florida, Alabama; Trump hits Tennessee midterms campaign trail.

item.title: Mike Ditka, former Chicago Bears head coach, dies at 86
item.description: Raised in a blue-collar Pennsylvania town, Mike Ditka earned a scholarship to Pitt and became "Da Coach" in Chicago. His family called him "the heart of our family" in announcing his death at 86.

item.title: Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan to be executed Dec. 3, email states
item.description: Nidal Hasan is set to die by firing squad in what will be the first military execution since 1961.

item.title: OpenAI halts model release over safety concerns: "Didn't quite meet the bar"
item.description: OpenAI said it has chosen not to release its new GPT-6.1 Astra model due to concerns about safety, as industry leaders warn of the risks posed by ever-more-powerful AI technology.
